state.case_summary:
A woman in her 70s with recurrent primary peritoneal carcinoma receiving pembrolizumab and ipilimumab presented with a pruritic rash ongoing for 2 weeks. The rash started as an erythematous papule on her right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen, then gradually enlarged and spread to involve both legs. She denied any new systemic symptoms associated with onset of the rash. A recent trial of oral terbinafine yielded no improvement.

Erythematous annular plaques without scale on her right arm and bilateral legs.

- Biopsy findings:  - 4-mm punch biopsy from right arm showed superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils  - Periodic acid–Schiff (PAS) stain was negative for fungal organisms- Images:  Image A Title: Erythematous annular plaques on left lower leg  Image A Description: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the left lower leg    Image B Title: Erythematous annular plaques on right lower leg    Image B Description: Erythematous annular plaques without scale on the right lower leg    Image C Title: Histopathology - Inflammation pattern  Image C Description: Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation    Image D Title: Histopathology - Eosinophils  Image D Description: Hematoxylin and eosin stain demonstrating numerous scattered eosinophils

root.label: Subacute Progressive Pruritic Rash with Perivascular Inflammation and Eosinophilia
supporting_facts: rash started as an erythematous papule on right arm 2 months after initiation of a new immunotherapy regimen
superficial and deep perivascular and interstitial inflammation with numerous eosinophils on biopsy
excluded_candidates: infection: negative PAS stain and lack of response to terbinafine make this less likely
allergic contact dermatitis: lack of clear exposure history and presence of eosinophils on biopsy make this less likely
salient_findings: erythematous annular plaques without scale on right arm and bilateral legs
numerous eosinophils on hematoxylin and eosin stain
negative PAS stain for fungal organisms
